chapter: MJQ, Pettiford and the move to Paris
title: Cannonball Adderley sits in at the Bohemia; his first record date
summary: A schoolteacher on vacation, Cannonball played Pettiford's new tune flawlessly; Clarke arranged a date with Ozzie Cadena at Rudy Van Gelder's the next day.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Cannonball Adderley: the sound, the man, the band

blocks.x: So that's the way it was. When Cannonball came to New York, on vacation, because he was a schoolteacher in Florida, and he came to New York on his vacation, the month of August, with his brother. So they came to the Bohemia, which was a place where everything was really happening, you know, with Oscar and all, and Duke Jordan had just written, (Singing), all those things. Everything was happening. Everything, like innovation was just all over the place. So they came there, and Oscar had just written, "Bohemia After Dark." So this little country boy, sitting out there with his alto under his arm, listening and listening and listening. Finally he comes up to me and touches me on the leg, because I was -- my drums were sitting up like this, so he would come to the bandstand and just touch my leg like that. So he came up to the bandstand and touched my leg. So I looked down, and he said, "Hey, Kenny, may I blow one?" I said, "Well, I'll ask Oscar." You know, because I was kind of skeptical, about people we didn't know, you know.
So I said, "Oscar, can he sit in?" Oscar said, "Not on this tune. I just wrote it yesterday. How

can he know it?" I said, "Okay, man. Okay, man." So in the meantime, I said, "Go ahead, man." So he began to take his horn out, and Oscar is playing, and says, "Klook Klue, what are you doing, man? I don't want the cat up here." I said, "Man, be cool, you know. You don't know." Boy, Cannonball came up on the stand and he played, "Bohemia After Dark," like he wrote it.
He just heard it the one time?

Just heard it. Man, he was such a fantastic musician. That's what he was, a music teacher. And he came up there, he played, "Bohemia After Dark," I said, "Well, who wrote it, you or Oscar?" And Oscar looked at him and said, "Boy, you are fantastic." So that was the beginning of Cannonball. So the next day he said, "Well, I'm living with my aunt and we have to get back, but I have no money, you know." So I said, "Tomorrow at 2:00 o'clock you have a record date." He said, "A record date?" I said, "That's right." So I called Ozzie Cadena right away and I said 2:00 o'clock tomorrow at Rudy Van Gelder's. He said okay. Said who you got? I said, don't worry, you'll see all the cats. Hank and Wendell Marshall, that's my rhythm section, but I found two other guys who played very well from Florida. He said, "Great, okay." 2:00 o'clock, we went out to Rudy Van Gelder's and made the first Cannonball date. And --
Yeah, we used Nat to, you know, kind of
back up Cannon, because they had been rehearsing together.
So then after, Nat made his own album, you know, and things began to spread out.

And so I told Cannonball, I said, "Now, you just wait right here, and as soon as we finish you'll get your check, you and Nat." So when we were finished, Ozzie said, -- I said, "Ozzie, where's the check for Cannon and Nat." So he says, "Right here. Right here." So I says, "Okay, here you are." They looked at the check and they looked at me and they said, "Oh, man, this is -- oh, Klook, you're so beautiful." And so we went through all that. So, about -- well, we recorded, you know, with Hank, and then we had -- you know, Wendell and then the other bass player, he's from home too, Paul Chambers.
And then we had -- always had Nat and Cannonball as much as we could, you know.
So they didn't go back to Florida.
They didn't? Well, how about that.
